summary: Runner startup blocked by inconsistent Vault token TTL after token rekey causing mixed auth state
description:
Issue summary: After last scheduled Vault token rekey (2026-03-12 03:00 UTC), a subset of on-demand CI runners failed to complete startup and reported authentication failures. Impact: ~12% of runner fleet in us-east failed to register; several queued release jobs timed out and were rescheduled. Root cause hypothesis: staggered token reissuance with different TTLs produced a transient 'split-brain' where some runners attempted to use old tokens and others received short-lived tokens and evicted cached credentials.

Impact details: Internal CI pipelines (release and nightly) experienced delays, ~25 release jobs retried, no customer-facing outages but release cadence impacted.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Perform a Vault token rekey with default orchestration script (no runner drain).
2) Trigger a new runner pod creation in k8s via CI autoscaler during rekey window.
3) Observe runner logs: auth failures with mismatched TTLs and repeated token refresh attempts.
logs: 2026-03-12T03:01:12Z runner-249 auth: token validation failed: token expired (received TTL 0s)
2026-03-12T03:01:13Z runner-174 auth: obtained token with TTL 15s, scheduled refresh at 2026-03-12T03:01:28Z
2026-03-12T03:01:28Z runner-174 auth: refresh failed: token revoked during rekey (403)
2026-03-12T03:02:02Z autoscaler: attempted to create 8 runner pods, 5 failed to register within 60s
investigation_notes: 03:10 UTC: Confirmed Vault rekey ran at 03:00 UTC using runbook 'vault/rotate-service-tokens' with no runner drain step configured.

03:25 UTC: Noticed two token issuance flows in logs: legacy long-lived tokens (TTL ~1h) and new short-lived tokens (TTL 15s) issued to different agents due to race in token propagation to token-signing nodes.
03:40 UTC: K8s node-level cache occasionally served stale token metadata to new pods created during rekey; cache invalidation lag ~20-40s.
04:00 UTC: Replicated locally by running rekey against staging Vault with simulated signer pool; reproduced mixed-TTL issuance when signer nodes processed requests during leader failover.

04:30 UTC: Hypothesis: rotation orchestration triggers signer reloads and leader election; during that window signing service returned inconsistent TTL defaults to clients. Runners that received very short TTL attempted immediate refresh and were rejected because old tokens were revoked mid-refresh.
comments: Maya Patel (reporter) - 2026-03-12T05:12Z: Initial alert from CI: large spike of runner-registration failures in us-east. Created ticket and attached preliminary logs.

Diego Ramos (assignee) - 2026-03-12T06:05Z: Investigating. Reproduced in staging with controlled rekey; caching layer and signer pool race looks likely. Will coordinate with Vault infra team and autoscaler owners.
SRE-Oncall (channel #infra) - 2026-03-12T07:00Z: Temporary mitigation applied: increased runner creation timeout and added backoff to CI scheduler to reduce burst during rekey windows.
Vault Team (comment) - 2026-03-12T08:30Z: Found that a recent change to the signer service altered default TTL when leader changes; reverting change for emergency rollback considered.
Diego Ramos - 2026-03-13T09:15Z: Rolled out a hotfix to the rotation script: add explicit signer quiesce and token TTL harmonization step; performing controlled rollout to prod-us-east.
resolution: Workaround: manually restart affected runner pods to pick up refreshed tokens and avoid stale cache; throttled autoscaler to reduce concurrent pod creation during rotation. Fix: updated vault rotation runbook to include signer quiesce, a 60s cache invalidation window, and harmonized TTL issuance before revoking old tokens. Deployed change to prod-us-east 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. Follow-ups: add automated drain of new-runner creation during rotation, add observability metric for signer TTL variance, and schedule a postmortem in Confluence (link provided).
